key_insight: Neural policy iteration with monotone finite differences tackles high-dimensional degenerate Hamilton–Jacobi equations without storing a global tensor grid.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a memory-efficient route to high-dimensional optimal-control and differential-game PDEs with rank-deficient diffusion.
method: Add artificial viscosity to obtain a monotone finite-difference operator.
Use neural networks and local stencil values to approximate linear policy-evaluation equations.
Bound propagated evaluation and optimization errors, and connect the scheme to the original equation through vanishing viscosity.
evidence_signal: On manufactured problems, mean errors beat direct PINNs at every tested dimension from 5 to 50 under equal training time; at 50 dimensions and 900 seconds, mean relative L2 error was about 40% lower across three paired seeds.
watch_item: Artificial viscosity introduces bias, so accuracy against the original degenerate equation requires refinement and independent validation.
paper_title: Finite-difference neural policy iteration for high-dimensional degenerate Hamilton--Jacobi equations
